rule_summary: Foster parents must be at least 25 years old.
notes: Rule of the MSF Fostering Scheme; the same on MSF's FAQ.

rule_summary: Applicants must be married and apply together as a couple.
notes: The SG Cares application needs a main applicant and a co-applicant (the spouse).

rule_summary: Applicants must be financially stable.
notes: No amount is given. See sg-sg-income-2.

rule_summary: There is no minimum household income for fostering applicants since July 2024. A household assessment still checks that the family can give care and stability.
notes: MSF press release of 23 August 2025. MSF gives the month only. Older pages still found online, such as a 2023 Boys' Town volunteer page, list a minimum household income of $2,000 a month.

rule_summary: There is no minimum education requirement for fostering applicants since July 2024.
notes: MSF press release of 23 August 2025. Older agency pages still list secondary school education.

rule_summary: Applicants must be medically fit to care for children. The assessment includes medical screening of both spouses.
Expatriates and foreigners may apply, but should stay in Singapore for the next 3 years.
notes: MSF answer on Ask.gov.sg. An MSF release of 2019 said applicants must be resident in Singapore; the current eligibility page does not mention residency.

rule_summary: Foster parents must provide a child-safe home. For children under 13, this includes window grilles on all windows.
notes: The value is the child's age below which grilles are needed.

rule_summary: Applicants who cannot or will not fit window grilles can foster only young people aged 13 and over.
notes: MSF answer on Ask.gov.sg.

rule_summary: Foster parents must not use physical punishment, such as caning or hitting.
notes: Listed as part of the child-safe home criterion. MSF's FAQ says physical punishment in any form is not allowed.

rule_summary: MSF or an MSF-appointed agency assesses each family. This includes interviews with the couple and all household members, including domestic helpers and tenants, a home visit and medical screening.
After the assessment, MSF decides on the application and tells the applicants the outcome.
notes: Boys' Town's page says its assessor sends a final report to an MSF panel.

rule_summary: The application and assessment take about three months.
notes: Boys' Town says 2 to 3 months; PPIS Oasis says up to 3 months.

rule_summary: Once approved, both spouses must complete foundation and intermediate training courses. Topics include bonding and attachment, grief and loss, abuse and trauma, and contact with birth families.
notes: Training comes after approval, before or alongside a first placement. Run by the Social Service Institute, usually on Saturday mornings. Hours not stated. The foundation course lists 8 modules.

rule_summary: Foster parents can also take specialised courses, such as the Positive Parenting Programme, and elective courses on parenting teenagers, working with birth parents and cyber wellness.
notes: No yearly training requirement was found.

rule_summary: In law, a foster parent is a person whom the Director-General or a protector thinks competent to care for a child, given their character, and who gives an undertaking to do so.
legal_citation: Children and Young Persons Act 1993, s 2(1) definition of 'foster parent', as amended by the Children and Young Persons (Amendment) Act 2019
notes: Read in the Children and Young Persons (Amendment) Bill 2019 (Bill No. 22/2019) on parliament.gov.sg. The amendments are now in the Children and Young Persons Act 1993 (2020 Revised Edition), where sections were renumbered; that text on sso.agc.gov.sg was not read (HTTP 403).

rule_summary: A Committee on Fostering, set up by the Minister, reviews cases of children placed with foster parents and advises whether each child's care plan is being followed.
legal_citation: Children and Young Persons Act 1993, Part on fostering (new s 27B in the 2019 amending Bill)
notes: Read in the Children and Young Persons (Amendment) Bill 2019 (Bill No. 22/2019) on parliament.gov.sg. The amendments are now in the Children and Young Persons Act 1993 (2020 Revised Edition), where sections were renumbered; that text on sso.agc.gov.sg was not read (HTTP 403).

rule_summary: The monthly fostering allowance for a child aged 0 to 12 is $1,100.
notes: Paid for each foster child to the main applicant. MSF raised it to this amount in 2022 (parliamentary answer, February 2025).

rule_summary: The monthly fostering allowance for a child aged 0 to 12 with special or medical needs is $1,500.
The monthly fostering allowance for a teenager aged 13 and over is $1,300, from October 2025.
notes: Up from $1,100 (MSF press release of 23 August 2025, which gives the month only).

rule_summary: The monthly fostering allowance for a teenager aged 13 and over with special or medical needs is $1,800, from October 2025.
notes: Up from $1,500 (MSF press release of 23 August 2025, which gives the month only).

rule_summary: After subsidies, foster parents pay a flat $200 a month for full-day infant care or childcare.
notes: Half-day care costs $150 a month. Applies generally at Anchor Operator and Partner Operator centres.

rule_summary: Foster parents pay a flat $80 a month at MSF-registered student care centres.
notes: MSF says the allowance is sized to cover this co-payment.

rule_summary: Every foster parent has a foster care worker, a 24-hour emergency hotline and access to respite care from another foster parent. Medical care at public healthcare institutions is subsidised.
Working foster parents can take childcare leave, as birth parents do.
legal_citation: Child Development Co-Savings Act, s 12B; Employment Act, s 87A (section numbers as given in the 2019 amending Bill)
notes: The 2019 amendment to the Children and Young Persons Act lets foster parents share information about the child where needed to claim this leave.

rule_summary: Each adoptive applicant must be at least 25 years old.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 5(1)(a)(i) and (b)(i)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. The court may still make an order in the cases in s 5(2).

rule_summary: Each applicant must be at least 21 years older than the child.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 5(1)(a)(ii) and (b)(ii)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. No upper age limit was found.

rule_summary: Only a married couple can adopt jointly. The marriage must be recognised in Singapore.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 4(1)(a) and (2)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. Marriages under the Administration of Muslim Law Act 1966 or the Women's Charter 1961, or recognised marriages abroad.

rule_summary: A single person may adopt alone. A married person adopting alone needs the spouse's consent, unless the court dispenses with it.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 4(1)(b), (2)(b) and s 5(2)(b)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. MSF's FAQ adds that a single person may adopt a child who was conceived naturally in Singapore.

rule_summary: A man applying alone cannot adopt a girl, unless special circumstances justify it.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 5(1)(c) and (2)(c)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. MSF's FAQ gives adopting his own biological child as an example.

rule_summary: Applicants must live in Singapore habitually. For a joint application, at least one spouse must be a citizen or both must be permanent residents. A sole applicant must be a citizen or permanent resident.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 4(1)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. MSF's page says foreigners can adopt jointly with a Singaporean spouse.

rule_summary: Applicants must have lived in Singapore for at least one continuous year before applying for an Adoption Suitability Assessment (ASA).
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 14(2)(a)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024.

rule_summary: Permanent residents, and foreigners adopting with a Singaporean spouse, should check that their home country will recognise a Singapore adoption order.
notes: MSF's FAQ also encourages permanent residents adopting a foreign child to adopt in their home country.

rule_summary: People convicted of offences prescribed in regulations, such as serious violent, sexual or drug offences, cannot adopt by default.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 5(1)(d); Adoption of Children (Prescribed Offences) Regulations 2024
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. The regulations are named in MSF's adoption handbook; their text was not read.

rule_summary: Prospective adopters are screened for risk factors, including criminal records, during the ASA.
notes: MSF parliamentary answer of 16 January 2024. TOUCH's ASA page lists physical, mental and criminal background checks.

rule_summary: During the court stage, MSF's social investigation includes checks with character referees and the applicants' support network.
notes: MSF parliamentary answer of 16 January 2024. No number of referees is stated.

rule_summary: The suitability checks for the ASA and the court stage include physical and mental health.
notes: MSF Adoption Handbook (October 2024).

rule_summary: The suitability checks include financial ability to support a child.
notes: MSF Adoption Handbook (October 2024). No amount is given.

rule_summary: All applicants must attend a Pre-Adoption Briefing run by an Authorised Adoption Agency. It must be within the 3 years before the court application, and before applying for an ASA.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 11(a), s 12 and s 14(2)(b)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. MSF's handbook says the briefing lasts about 2 hours, in English or Mandarin.

rule_summary: All applicants must also attend a briefing on telling the child about the adoption, within the 3 years before the court application.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 11(b) and s 13
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. MSF's pages say both briefings come before the ASA application.

rule_summary: Applicants need a valid, favourable Adoption Suitability Assessment from an Authorised Adoption Agency before applying to court. It replaced the Home Study Report.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 11(c) and s 14
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. MSF's page says a favourable ASA is needed before identifying a child, and is followed by a Letter of Eligibility from the agency.

rule_summary: The ASA looks at the home, motivation to adopt, views on parenting, risk of harm to a child and ability to provide for a child.
notes: MSF answer on Ask.gov.sg. Agency pages say it involves interviews, screenings and home visits.

rule_summary: An agency takes on average 5 to 8 weeks to complete an ASA, counted from the first interview.
notes: MSF answer on Ask.gov.sg. No single value, because the time is a range. Longer for complex cases.

rule_summary: The Guardian-in-Adoption's investigation after the court application usually takes up to 9 months for straightforward cases.
notes: MSF answer on Ask.gov.sg. The court then usually fixes a hearing within a month.

rule_summary: A favourable ASA is valid for 2 years from the date it is issued.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 20(1)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024.

rule_summary: An ASA covers one adoption only. A new ASA is needed for a later adoption.
notes: MSF Adoption Handbook (October 2024).

rule_summary: Applicants can ask the agency that did their ASA to extend it, from 3 months before it expires.
notes: LCCS says an extension gives another 2 years and costs $150 with no material changes.

rule_summary: MSF describes five types of adoption: a biological child, a stepchild, a relative such as a niece or nephew, an unrelated child, and a child in state care.
notes: ASA fees differ for related and unrelated children (see the fees rows).

rule_summary: The court may set aside the age rules when the applicant and the child are close blood relatives.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 5(2)(a)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. The Act says 'within the prohibited degrees of consanguinity'.

rule_summary: The court may make an adoption order despite an eligibility rule if special circumstances justify it as an exceptional measure. It considers whether the Guardian-in-Adoption supports the order.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 5(2)(c) and (3)
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024.

rule_summary: An adoption order can only be made for a child under 21 who has never married and is resident in Singapore.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 6
notes: Read in the Bill as introduced (Bill No. 12/2022) on parliament.gov.sg. The enacted text on Singapore Statutes Online was not read: sso.agc.gov.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403). MSF's FAQ cites the same section numbering. The Act came into force on 15 October 2024. A child on a visit, student or special pass does not count as resident. The under-21 rule is from MSF's page and the handbook.

rule_summary: An unrelated child must not live with prospective adopters before they hold a favourable ASA, and, for a foreign child, approval in principle of a Dependant's Pass.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, s 57
notes: Does not apply to stepchildren, relatives or foster children placed under the Children and Young Persons Act. Section number from the Bill as introduced.

rule_summary: Adoption agencies must publish the amounts they charge. Payments for an adoption are allowed only for permitted purposes.
legal_citation: Adoption of Children Act 2022, ss 54 and 55
notes: Section numbers from the Bill as introduced. The handbook lists the permitted payments.

rule_summary: An ASA for adopting an unrelated or relative's child costs $2,000.
notes: Charged by the Authorised Adoption Agency. TOUCH and Fei Yue list $2,180 including GST; LCCS lists $2,000 GST exempt.

rule_summary: An ASA for adopting a biological child or stepchild costs $1,100, plus $315 for each extra child adopted at the same time.
notes: TOUCH and Fei Yue list $1,199 including GST.

rule_summary: MSF's FAQ gives $50 a person, or $100 a couple, for each group briefing.
notes: Agency pages read the same day list higher rates; see sg-sg-fees-4.

rule_summary: LCCS charges $75 a person, or $150 a couple, for each group briefing from May 2026.
notes: GST exempt. ACOSS lists $75; TOUCH and Fei Yue list $81.75 including GST.

rule_summary: A Dependant's Pass for a foreign child costs $330. The pass lasts 21 months.
notes: MSF Adoption Handbook (October 2024). A $30 visa fee may apply. MSF processes an application within 20 working days of a complete submission. Extensions cost $225 (MSF FAQ).

rule_summary: MSF charges $250 for the Guardian-in-Adoption's investigation and affidavit.
notes: Legal fees, and medical or psychological reports asked for during the investigation, are extra.
